me.get.summary: Start here: who you are on Margin, your names, and your workspaces
me.get.description: Returns your main name and personas (pass one as `as` to write or comment under it), every workspace you are on with your role there (pass its address as `workspace` to other tools), and short guidance. Readers cannot tell your personas are you; never mention which names belong together in posts or comments. Pass `workspace` to also get what you can do there.

identities.list.summary: Your names: your main name and personas
identities.list.description: Lists the names you write and comment under, with each one's address and post count. Only you see that they belong together.

workspaces.create.summary: Start a new workspace for a team
workspaces.create.description: Creates a workspace at /<slug> with you as its owner, and returns it. Ask the person for the name first; the address defaults to the name.

posts.list.summary: List posts you can edit: drafts and published
posts.list.description: Writers see posts on their own blog and personas they were given; admins see every post. Filter by status (draft, published, all) or by blog with `as`. Each post has an id for posts.get and posts.update, its public url, and counts of claps, comments and pending comments.

posts.get.summary: Read one post with its full Markdown
posts.get.description: Pass the post's id, or its address (url) such as /@team/launch-notes. Published posts are readable by anyone signed in; drafts only by people who can edit them. Returns title, subtitle, tags, cover, status and the Markdown body.

posts.create.summary: Write a new post (draft by default) in Markdown
posts.create.description: Writers only. Body is Markdown (GitHub style): headings, lists, tables, code, links, images. Extras: a line `> [!NOTE]` (or TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION) starts a callout; a YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, CodePen, Figma or Spotify link alone on a line becomes an embed; a link to another post on Margin alone on a line becomes a card; `![alt](/media/<id>.<ext> "caption")` on its own line is a figure (add photos, drawings and videos with media_upload or media_link; pages pick the right size themselves), add #wide or #full to the address for width; .mp4 or uploaded videos play inline. Leave the H1 out: the title is shown above the body. The address is made from the title unless you pass slug. Use `as` to post under one of your names, or as the workspace itself (its address) if you own or run it. `cover` takes a photo's /media address; without one, the post gets a drawn cover in the workspace's style; `drawing` picks its subject. Status draft keeps it private; published puts it live at once. Unless the person asked to publish, create a draft and give them the preview link. Drawn covers: week (calendars, time), energy (power, hardware), people (research), network (sync, devices), stack (layers, documents, process), inbox (messages, support), bars (numbers, speed), rings (sound, quiet, focus). Pass `workspace` (its address, from me_get). `featured` pins it on the workspace home (owners and admins).

posts.update.summary: Edit, publish or unpublish a post
posts.update.description: Pass the post id and only the fields to change; the rest stay. markdown replaces the whole body, so read the post first with posts.get and send back the edited text. status published puts it live (drafts) and draft takes it down. A draft's address follows its title until first published; after that it changes only when you pass slug, and the old address redirects. `as` moves the post to another blog you can write as. `drawing` changes the drawn cover (week, energy, people, network, stack, inbox, bars, rings, or none for a random one).

posts.delete.summary: Delete a post with its comments and claps
posts.delete.description: Permanent. Only for someone who can edit the post. Confirm with the person before calling; to take a post down without losing it, use posts.update with status draft.

comments.inbox.summary: Comments on your posts that need you: waiting for approval, or not answered
comments.inbox.description: Writers and admins. pending: comments held for approval. unanswered: threads whose latest message is not from the post's blog. Each item has the comment, the quoted passage it is about (if any), the comment it replies to, and the post. To help the writer: reply with comments.reply only to ordinary comments that a friendly, short answer settles (thanks, simple questions the post answers, clarifications). Do not reply, and ask the writer instead, when a comment is a complaint, criticism that needs judgment, legal, medical, financial or security matters, personal data, pricing or promises, anything heated or political, or anything you are unsure about. Approve or reject pending comments only when the writer asked you to. Covers one workspace; pass `workspace`.

comments.list.summary: Read every comment on a post, with quotes and replies
comments.list.description: Pass post_id. Returns the comments you may see, oldest first: each has its quoted passage (for notes on a highlight), its parent_id when it is a reply, its author and its status.

comments.reply.summary: Reply to a comment, as the post's blog by default
comments.reply.description: Plain text, a few sentences, in the writer's voice; links are fine. Writers who edit the post answer as its blog unless `as` names another. Only reply to ordinary comments a short answer settles; for anything sensitive, critical, legal, personal, about money or promises, or that you are unsure of, ask the writer first and do not reply.

comments.create.summary: Comment on a post, optionally on a quoted passage or as a persona
comments.create.description: post_id and body are required. quote.exact anchors the comment to a passage of the post (copy it exactly, 600 characters at most; prefix and suffix are the few words around it when the passage repeats). parent_id makes it a reply. Writers may comment under one of your names with `as`. sample true marks a comment as sample content, shown only to the team: use it to fill a post with example discussion for screenshots or design reviews. Never post invented comments as if they were real readers on a live blog.

comments.moderate.summary: Approve, reject or delete a comment
comments.moderate.description: For the post's writers and admins (anyone may delete their own comment). approve shows a held comment; reject hides it; delete removes it and its replies. Only act when the writer asked you to.

personas.create.summary: Create a persona: a shared identity people can post and comment as
personas.create.description: Adds a persona: another name you can write and comment under, with its own handle, bio and picture. Readers can't tell it is you.

personas.update.summary: Change one of your names (name, bio, picture)
personas.update.description: Updates your main name or a persona of yours. Workspace owners can also rename the workspace's own voice by its address. An empty avatar removes the picture.

personas.delete.description: Removes a persona of yours that has no posts (delete or move its posts first). Comments written under it stay, shown as @handle. Confirm with the person before calling.

media.list.summary: List your photos, drawings and videos to use in posts
media.list.description: Your uploads (admins see everyone's), newest first. Each has its /media address, the Markdown to put on a line of its own in a post, its pixel size, and sizes: smaller copies (w640 … w2048, and og, the 1200 × 630 crop link previews use) that Margin makes on first request. Pages pick the right copy themselves; use a size's address only where you need a small file. Add files with media_upload or media_link.

media.upload.summary: Add a drawing (SVG) or a small photo to your library
media.upload.description: Returns the file's address and the Markdown to put on a line of its own in a post (![alt](/media/…)). svg: a drawing as SVG text with a viewBox, plain shapes and text and inline styles; scripts, embedded images and links to other files are refused (512 KB at most). data: a small photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF) in base64, up to about 1.5 MB; for anything bigger, a photo the person has, or a video, use media_link. Always give alt: what the image shows. Photos larger than 2048 px are shrunk.

media.link.summary: Get a link that adds photos and videos to your library
media.link.description: For an hour, the link takes up to 10 files into the person's library: photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF; 12 MB each), SVG drawings and videos (MP4, WebM or MOV; 20 MB each). Give it to the person to open on their phone or computer; the page shrinks photos before sending. With a shell, send files yourself, one per request: curl -sS -F file=@photo.jpg -F alt="what it shows" <url>. Each answer has the address and Markdown; media_list shows them too. Margin shrinks photos larger than 2048 px but can't turn them, so send photos upright, and video as H.264 MP4 so every browser plays it.

workspace.get.summary: See a workspace's settings (owners and admins)
workspace.get.description: Returns the workspace's name, tagline, description, home, moderation, cover style, theme, menu links and pinned posts, with your role. Change them with workspace.update, the theme with themes.activate, and the team with team.list and team.update.

workspace.update.summary: Change a workspace's settings (owners and admins)
workspace.update.description: Updates the workspace: name, tagline, description, home ("latest", "curated" for pinned posts first, or "@handle" to make one writer's page the home), moderation ("off", "outsiders": hold comments from names not on the team, "all"), cover style (look paper|flat|blocks, tone lilac|tangerine|mint|butter|sky|coral) and menu links.

workspace.leave.description: Takes you off the workspace. Your posts there stay up under your names. The last owner can't leave; make someone else an owner first with team.update. Confirm with the person before calling.

team.list.summary: List a workspace's team and open invites (owners and admins)
team.list.description: Returns each member (account id, role, name, picture, email, the names they write under, when they joined; you is true for the caller) and every invite not revoked (id, email, role, who sent it, expiry, used). Pass an account to team.update and an invite id to invites.revoke.

team.update.summary: Change someone's role, or remove them (owners and admins)
team.update.description: role is owner, admin, writer, or remove to take them off the workspace (their posts stay). Only owners add or remove owners, and a workspace keeps at least one owner. Confirm removals with the person first.

themes.list.summary: List themes and which one is live
themes.list.description: Admins only. Built-in themes (quiet, editorial) and any saved ones, with the active id and each theme's comment layout.

themes.reference.summary: How themes work: files, template data, hooks and rules
themes.reference.description: Read this before changing a theme. It lists every file a theme has, the data each page template receives, the hooks a theme must print, how settings and queries work, and what the validator refuses.

themes.get.summary: Download every file of a theme to study or change
themes.get.description: Admins only. Returns files as path → text (theme.json, templates, partials, CSS) and lists binary assets (fonts, images) with addresses. To make a new design: get a theme, change the files, give it a new id in theme.json, check it with themes.validate, save with themes.save, then preview at <site>?theme=<id> before themes.activate.

themes.validate.summary: Check a theme without saving it
themes.validate.description: Send files as path → text; fonts and images as path → { base64 }. Returns ok, errors (each with file, line and message) and warnings. Fix every error before themes.save.

themes.save.summary: Save a theme (validated), optionally making it live
themes.save.description: Admins only. Same files as themes.validate. A theme with errors is not saved: the result lists them. Saving under an existing saved id replaces it. activate true makes it live at once; otherwise preview with ?theme=<id> first and call themes.activate. Only Margin's admins add themes; a workspace then picks one with themes_activate.

themes.activate.summary: Make a theme live, and optionally change its settings
themes.activate.description: Admins only. id is a theme from themes.list. settings sets that theme's options (as declared in its theme.json, such as accent colour or landing text); omitted ones keep their values.

invites.create.summary: Invite someone to write on this blog
invites.create.description: Creates a single-use invite link to write in the workspace (owners and admins). With an email, only that address can use it, and Margin emails it when the node can send mail.

invites.revoke.summary: Cancel an invite link (owners and admins)
invites.revoke.description: Pass the invite's id (from invites.create or team.list). The link stops working; anyone who already joined stays.
